defects.defect: Wave A is drawn at the ceiling of one plan: 48 steps by its own count, about 50 steps and 24 hours by mine, and only with S6, S9 and S14 all taken. It also defers the roadmap's coded check on who may call the mail connector (S1) without listing S1 among the simplifications it relies on; with that check the proposal itself says Jordan's inbox or the lookup must move to wave B.

Eight ids and three new kinds of risk in one plan; seven of the eight are built only if Tony answers Q6, Q4, Q2 and Q10, and calendar answers, the evening text and the handbook are things he has not asked for. It is one plan only with S5, S8, S10 and S11 and every answer yes (about 21.5 hours and 41 steps by my count) and about 10 hours if the answers are no, so it cannot be written as a plan until he answers.

G009 is counted as placed, but only its pin on the scheduling tool is built; the card's own function, a text to the other parent, stays off unless Tony reverses his roadmap rule on sends into other conversations. The count of 19 placed cards overstates what the family gets by one.

Both things the roadmap's research milestone adds beyond the web helper, trip planning and email to the asker, are left out. The reason given for F049 is that nobody on record asked for it, although that milestone is titled 'Research & trips, email to the asker'; F028's small form is about two hours and fits wave B.
The exit test needs a reminder to fire, but reminders are built only if Q6 is answered yes; no exit test is given for the wave without them.

'Did I get an email about X?', half of the card Tony asked to have in wave A, goes live in wave B. The record of 11 Oct moves the whole-inbox features, the 07:00 text and the lookup, together with the school digest, and by this proposal's own figures the lookup fits in A only if Jordan's inbox or the envelope gives way; moving it also creates what its own note calls the riskiest combination in A to C at the end of B.

Seven cards of which only F041 is unconditional; the rest wait on Q6, Q4, Q2 and Q10, and calendar answers, the evening text and the handbook are things Tony has not asked for. With every answer yes it is 44 steps and about 23 hours by my count, at the ceiling, and only with S5, S8, S10 and S11.

The headline size (21 hours, 43 steps) covers Tony's inbox only, although the wave draws Jordan's inbox as a phase; with it I count about 24 hours and 47 steps, and with the envelope 50 steps, so the wave as drawn has no room left.
Placed with no condition listed, although it ships only as one line on the printed sheet (S14); as the card is written it needs family delivery (G009), which this proposal leaves out of every wave.
Four go-live phases, and one plan only with S7, S13 and S15: 35 hours as the cards are written against 20 simplified, where the deps cut of the same wave fits as written.

Left out on the strength of S14, which Tony has not confirmed, although the proposal's own notes make it step one of any plan for the two advanced abilities he named; it is config only and about an hour.
The exit test needs a reminder to fire although reminders are built only if Q6 is answered yes; the rules phase says what is built on a no, but the exit test does not.

The reasons say Tony's two advanced examples were 'answered no' and 'not now'; those were the assistant's verdict and the review's removals, and nothing in the fact sheet shows Tony accepting them. This is also the one proposal whose notes never tell him that his third level has nothing in A to C, and it drops MAC-04, the one-hour gate both would start from.

The roadmap's coded check on who may call the mail connector is left to wave C by default, which is simplification S1, yet S1 is not in the wave's relies-on list (the text prices it at 3 hours). By my count the wave with that check is about 24 hours and 46 steps against its 22.5 and 44, so 'still one plan' is tighter than stated.

The lookup is named as the part to drop first if the plan runs long, though it is half of the mail card Tony asked for; Jordan's inbox, which waits on Q7 and whose school mail Tony's inbox already covers, is the better phase to give way.

Hours look light: a deny-by-default firewall, the Google project, the connector and the sign-in in 3.5 hours, and a 2.5-hour exit gate where M1 planned 3. I count about 21 hours and 41 steps against its 19.5 and 39; it still fits.

Calendar answers are the only item in wave B that rests on a family fact Tony has not given (Q4), and they add private calendar text to a wave that already adds web pages and attachments. The 'only if Q4' condition is right, but the phase sits before outings; as the last phase the wave would close cleanly without it.
The relies-on list names only S13, but the 18-hour figure also takes S7 and S15. With S13 alone and the calendar phase built I count about 24 hours, near the ceiling.

Four of the five cards wait on Q6, Q2 and Q3, so the wave is notes alone (about 10 hours) if the answers are no, and its exit test needs a reminder that Q6 may rule out. 'Email me this' also assumes an address for Happy to send from, which is not on record, and the 19-hour figure takes trims (facts in two places under S8, no send cap) that the relies-on list does not name.

Twenty-five of 42 ids are not in a wave, the longest list of the three, shown as one flat list resting mostly on Q3, which Tony has not answered; on 12 Oct he turned down 'the rest a pick list'. The list should say what comes after C and what answer unlocks each group, starting with the three the proposal itself says could join a wave cheaply.

In wave A install the firewall with the single rule that lets the mail connector reach Google only, and move deny-by-default for every program to wave B's gate phase; that frees roughly the time the coded check costs, so A stays one plan.

The overflow rule for wave A, applied to Jordan's inbox only: if A runs long, her inbox (already conditional on Q7) becomes the first phase of wave B without touching A's exit test, and the lookup stays in A with the 07:00 text.

Lay out wave B so its first phases are the deps cut (gate, web helper, photos and PDFs, hourly weather), which is one plan even as the cards are written, and make want's calendar and outing phases the trailing ones that need Q4 and the F028 cuts.
MAC-04 (about an hour, config only) in wave B's gate phase, named as the standing gate for the two advanced abilities Tony gave as examples, leaving the wave only if he takes S14.

The plain statement that Tony's two advanced examples are a plan of their own after C, and the grouping of the items not in a wave into the later plans they would form (Happy acts outside the chat; a paired device, MAC-04 first; the kids' agent after local models), in place of want's 'answered no' and 'not now' wording.

The note that waves B and C can swap if Tony would rather have notes and reminders before web reading, with the points that change (the flyer-photo route, the planted page and PDF test cases and, in the want base, the emailed outing plan).
